chapter: Baton Rouge heroes: Guy Kelly and Buddy Petit
title: Guy Kelly's records and Joe leaving him behind in Baton Rouge
summary: Barry and Joe discuss Guy Kelly's few records with Jimmie Noone; Joe left Kelly in Baton Rouge when he went with the Original Dixieland Jazz Band in 1924.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, Guy Kelly. Everybody says, 'Guy Kelly from New Orleans,' but as you were saying, he came from Scotland or...
Let me ask you a little more about Guy, because there's a very interesting subject. He died so young, and so many people swear by him...
If Guy had lived... He made a few records, I'm not sure if you know the records he made...

The ones he made with Jimmie Noone and Preston Jackson and Johnny Lindsay and whatnot. He made four sides there. I'm trying to think what else did Guy Kelly do. Some people say he's on a couple of those

Celestin things, but they can't be sure. Now, I know he played with Celestin... But when you heard Guy play in the early days, judging from the Jimmie Noone records you say you've heard... Was that a good example of Guy's playing, or...?

Well, somebody according... He was playing just as... I left Guy in Baton Rouge, in fact. When I left Baton Rouge to go with the Dixieland Rhythm Kings, the Original Dixieland Jazz Band I mean, Guy was still in Baton Rouge, and I think he was playing with... Maybe he was playing with Toots. I don't know. I can't remember. But I know he was still there.
He stayed with Toots for quite some while as far as I can remember.
And believe me, he could play good then, but he still wasn't a Louis. Because if he was, I never would have got so excited when I first referred to Louis.
